transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you too, and, um, thank you for taking the time to see me. I really appreciate it. 

I guess... well, I'm here because I mostly just don't feel like myself anymore? I hope I'm explaining this okay. It's probably nothing major, but I've sort of stopped doing the things I usually enjoy. Like hiking, or coaching, playing my guitar... I haven't even been calling people back lately. 

I feel a little embarrassed to admit this, but some days I just sit in my small rental for hours. I know there are things I need to do, but I just can't seem to make myself start. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Have you ever felt this way during any other period in your life before now?

Um, no, not really. I've always been a pretty motivated guy, you know? But... well, I guess things started sort of... unraveling a bit, about a year and two months ago? 

I feel a little bad even bringing personal stuff into this, but that was right after my divorce. I had just moved into that smaller rental I mentioned, and... I don't know, it's just been since then. It's probably just a normal rut, and I'm really trying my best to push through it, I promise. I hope that answers your question? Am I giving you the right details?
Looking back over your entire life, even long before the divorce, can you recall any other times where you felt this low, lost interest in things, or struggled to get through the day like this?

Um, I really appreciate you being so thorough, Dr. Smith. I want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need. 

Thinking back... no. Honestly, no. I've always tried to be the kind of guy people can count on. You know, in my line of work, you kind of have to be the steady one, right? 

Before all this started last year, I really never had any trouble getting out of bed or, you know, getting through the day. I was always pretty upbeat. I hope that's okay? I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm making a huge deal out of a little slump right now, it's just... this is really the first time I've ever felt quite this stuck. Is that the kind of background you were looking for?
Since this started, have you noticed any changes in how you sleep?

Um, sleep? Well, I mean... I think my sleep is mostly okay? I really try to keep a good schedule, you know, because of my job. I want to make sure I'm rested and ready if I get called in. 

I guess maybe I've been sleeping a little bit more than usual lately? But not a crazy amount or anything. Just... maybe an extra hour here or there when I'm feeling a bit tired. I hope that's not a bad thing? I really try not to let it get in the way of anything important. Does that sound fairly normal to you? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture.
Over the past year, would you say you have felt this way nearly every single day, or have there been significant periods of time where you felt completely like your old self again?

Um, well... I really want to give you the right answer here. I guess... it's been pretty constant? I mean, I really try to put on a brave face, you know, especially for work. I don't want anyone to think I'm slacking off or can't handle my responsibilities. 

But, if I'm being completely honest, and I hope it's okay to say this... I haven't really felt like my old self much at all this past year. I keep hoping I'll just snap out of it, and I really am trying, I promise. But it just sort of hangs around, almost every day. I hope that doesn't make me sound weak or anything? I'm just trying to be as accurate as I can for you. Is that the kind of information you need?
Have you noticed any change in your appetite or your weight since you started feeling this way?

Um, appetite? Well... I think I've been eating okay, mostly. I mean, I always try to make sure I eat enough to keep my strength up, especially with the job. You have to be ready for anything, right? 

I haven't really noticed any big changes in my weight, I don't think. Maybe my clothes fit a tiny bit differently, but nothing major. I really try to stay on top of things like that. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I haven't been keeping a strict log or anything, but I can start if you think I should. I just want to make sure I'm doing everything I'm supposed to be doing. Does that sound okay to you?
Do you often find yourself feeling worthless or guilty about the way you've been feeling lately?

Um, worthless? Oh, no, I wouldn't use a strong word like that. I mean, I have a really important job, you know? People rely on me to keep them safe, so I try to focus on that. I want to be useful and do my part. 

As for feeling guilty... well, maybe just a little bit? Sometimes I feel bad if I'm not, you know, operating at a hundred percent for the team. But I really try not to let myself wallow in it or anything. I just try to push through and do my best, because I know people are counting on me. I hope that's the right attitude to have? I'm really trying to stay positive about everything. Does that sound like a healthy way to handle it?
Have you noticed if your movements or your speech have slowed down, or conversely, if you've felt more restless or fidgety than usual lately?

Um, slowed down? No, no, I don't think so. I really try to stay sharp, you know? In my line of work, you can't afford to be sluggish, so I make sure I'm always moving at a good pace. I want to be ready for whatever comes up. 

And restless... well, maybe just a tiny bit sometimes? But nothing out of the ordinary, I promise. Just the normal amount of energy you need to stay alert on the job. I definitely try not to fidget or look nervous, because I want people to feel confident in me. I hope I'm presenting myself well here, too? I'm really trying to give you the clearest picture I can. Is that the kind of thing you're looking for?
During these past months, have you ever felt that life is not worth living or had thoughts about harming yourself?

Um, harming myself? Oh, gosh, no. No, definitely not. I mean, life is... well, it's very important, isn't it? I have a duty to my job and to the people I protect. I would never, ever do anything to jeopardize that or let anyone down like that. 

I really try to keep my mind focused on the mission, you know? Staying strong and capable. I would never want you to think I was... unstable in that way, or a risk to myself. I'm very committed to doing the right thing. I hope that puts your mind at ease? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right impression, that I'm taking all of this very seriously. Does that sound like a good answer?
Have you noticed any difficulty with your concentration or your ability to make decisions since you started feeling this way?

Um, concentration? Oh, I think my concentration is just fine. I mean, maybe there are moments where I get a little distracted, but who doesn't, right? Especially when there's so much going on around you. But I always pull it right back. I have to, for my job. I can't afford to miss anything, so I make sure I'm always paying close attention to my surroundings. 

And making decisions... I think I'm still pretty decisive. I try to weigh the options quickly and just do what needs to be done. I don't want to be the kind of person who hesitates when it matters. Sometimes it's a lot of pressure, but I really try to handle it well. I hope that's what you'd expect from someone in my line of work? I'm just trying to be as capable as I can be. Am I explaining that okay?
